expects.rule: The first screen shows who the person is, what they do and real work, not an intro animation. Users spent 57% of viewing time above the fold in NN/g's 2018 study.
Body and caption text reaches a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text), including grey text on photographs.
Menu links, filters and contact links are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or spaced so they are easy to hit on a phone.
Each project has a title, a year, the person's role and a way to open it as a page of its own that can be shared by link.
Contact (email or form) is reachable from every page without scrolling back to the top.
Work is shown at a size where it can be judged: images are not cropped to thumbnails smaller than about a third of the screen width on desktop.
The site stays usable without hover: project names and filters work by touch and keyboard (all functionality operable through a keyboard interface).

traits: 4 of 8 use a single typeface family (Fred Lord, Sam Thies, Félix Péault, Kalok Yeung); the other 4 use two, often a serif or mono beside a grotesque.
3 of 8 (Sam Thies, Maximilian Kaspar, Carter Ogunsola) set the interface in a monospace.
6 of 8 show work on the first screen: a full-bleed photo or video (Olivia Plender, Sam Thies, Alicia Dubuis), a scatter or grid of images (Fred Lord, Félix Péault), or a project frame (Kalok Yeung).
Navigation is two or three links, in small text, on 6 of 8 (Index, About or Info, News, Projects, Series).
The first screen carries one to three sentences of text on 6 of 8; case-study copy is on project pages.
3 of 8 have a dark background (#171209, #121212, #1e1e1e) and 3 a white or near-white one; Olivia Plender is a full photograph and Félix Péault a gradient. Colour comes from the work.
3 of 8 (Fred Lord, Alicia Dubuis, Kalok Yeung) show an email address on the first screen.
Projects are listed as an index with number, title, tags or year on 4 of 8 (Fred Lord, Alicia Dubuis, Maximilian Kaspar, Carter Ogunsola).

sites.name: Frédéric Lord
sites.why: Dark brown (#171209) page, all in Inter at small size: header with name and clock, Index and Information links, a short intro with email, then project screenshots scattered at different sizes with numbered captions and a table of number, project, industry, type and year.

sites.name: Olivia Plender
sites.why: Full-bleed film still of women aiming wooden guns, with seven project titles centred over it in white Excelsior serif; header has the name, Index, News and About in a small sans-serif. No other text; the image is the page.

sites.name: Sam Thies
sites.why: Full-bleed video of a dirt road seen through a windscreen, with one centred tagline and a three-link nav (Projects, Shop, About) in small monospace type (Quadrant Text Mono) over it. Page background #121212; project tiles come after the video.

sites.name: Alicia Dubuis
sites.why: White top bar with name, 'Photographer & Director', agent, email, Read More and an Overview / Index switch; a full-width close photograph of two soaps fills the screen under it. Jannon serif with ABC Camera Plain. The Index view lists numbered projects with date range and image count.

sites.name: Félix Péault
sites.why: Blue-to-green gradient over a pale pink (#f7eeec) page: one centred street photograph, huge F and P letters down the left edge, Series, Elsewhere and Info at right, and a centred 45 px bold statement. All in Suisse Intl Condensed. A grid of titled image links follows.

sites.name: Maximilian Kaspar
sites.why: White page ruled into four columns, name, photos and about in small monospace at top, and a 100 px lowercase headline set in Bugrino stating the job and employer at the bottom. No image on the first screen; Neue Montreal for text. A project list with title, tags, year and a plus icon follows.

sites.name: Carter Ogunsola
sites.why: Charcoal (#1e1e1e) screen with a 100% counter while it loads, then live status lines (clock, load time, people online) in PP Neue Montreal Mono and Oracle. Nav of About, Lab, Writing, Studio, Contact, command-K search, a Light/Dark/System switch, and 17 selected works as a text list.

sites.name: Kalok Yeung
sites.why: White page: a narrow left column with name and tagline in grey, a project list with colour swatches and a blue button carrying the email address; the rest is a tall portrait screenshot of one project in a black frame, with a feed below. All in Kern.

avoid: A full-screen intro or loader that hides the work for several seconds.
A hero with a slogan such as 'I craft digital experiences' and no project visible on the first screen.
A grid of identical rounded cards with the same shadow and a gradient, as in common portfolio templates.
Custom cursors or scroll hijacking that break normal scrolling, keyboard use or touch.
Project images without text alternatives or captions, and thumbnails too small to judge the work.
Contact only through a hover menu or a form with no visible email address.
Skill bars and percentage charts for abilities.

sources.name: Nielsen Norman Group, Scrolling and Attention
